Athena's fails-without run of the same command exited 101 with the fix reverted. I used --target because the shared default build directory held a stale athena-data artifact.

findings.summary: Two changed files are not on the expected deliverables list: reading.rs and briefs.rs.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat shows both files changed. The deliverables list does not name them, but the accepted plan does. The edits keep relax/remove records out of retry seeds and out of the producer's class summary, so a producer is never prompted to weaken the check that judges it. Each edit is small, tested, and tied to the feature.

findings.summary: The gate name is stored as a '[gate: NAME] ' prefix inside the free-text prevention field, not as a typed field.
findings.evidence: mark_prevention and gate_of_prevention put structured data inside a free-text field. Hestia parses the prefix back out, and status and review show it raw. The code and docs call this a stopgap that keeps the athena.introspection/1 shape unchanged. The cleaner fix is an optional typed `gate` field in a later schema revision.

findings.summary: When the base moved, 'same change' compares the list of changed files (path, status, mode, size) without hashing their contents, so it can report false disagreements.
findings.evidence: same_change uses this comparison only when the two base fingerprints differ. Two different edits of the same size to the same files would count as an overruling. The module comment, CHANGELOG and defaults-loop.md §3.8 all disclose this weakness. Adding a per-file content hash to the candidate's change entries would make the signal exact.

summary: The candidate does what the request asks. A new module, crates/athena-core/src/gate_counts.rs, reads the existing job records and counts, for each gate, the jobs it ended and the times a later "try again on <job>" landed the same change. Those counts now reach the introspection prompt, which says a rule or check can be wrong. The prevention_kind field accepts `relax` and `remove`, but only for a gate that later tries overruled at least once. Hestia queues one normal-priority request per such gate, citing its counts, and `athena status` lists the gates most overruled first. Every planned demonstration I ran passed. That covers 13 counter tests, the Hestia gate_review tests, the introspect, reading and briefs tests, 81 records tests, the CLI review tests, and 8 CLI introspection tests, including the run of the status binary. fmt, clippy and the full test suite passed in Athena's recorded CI run. One thing about my environment, not the change: in the shared build directory, every default-target cargo command failed to compile athena-context because a stale athena-data artifact had no `loosens`, even after a rebuild. The source does have `loosens`, and CI passed on this commit. So I ran every test with `--target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`, which forces a clean build of this tree in a separate directory. Also, `status --snapshot` prints only the job counts, history and throughput sections, so I could not see the gate section on the real records; that part is shown only by the fixture tests. Remaining findings are minor: reading.rs and briefs.rs changed, which the plan listed but the deliverables list did not, and two design shortcuts the docs admit to (the gate name is stored as a text prefix, and a moved-base match ignores file contents).
